sheets.title: The NCLEX at a Glance
sheets.hook: What the NCLEX actually looks like in 2026
sheets.pin_title: NCLEX 2026 Explained: Questions, Time Limit, Test Plan %
sheets.pin_desc: NCLEX-RN at a glance for 2026: 85 to 150 questions, 5 hours, 3 case studies, computer adaptive. Plus the 8 client needs categories and their percentages. Save this NCLEX study guide cheat sheet for nursing school.
facts: Ends when it's 95% sure you pass or fail
sheets.caption: The NCLEX in one page: 85–150 questions, 5 hours, 3 case studies, and it adapts to you. The number of questions you get tells you nothing, so don't panic at 85 or 150. Save this for later.

sheets.title: Clinical Judgment, Step by Step
sheets.hook: Every NCLEX case study follows these 6 steps
sheets.pin_title: NCLEX Clinical Judgment Model: The 6 Steps Explained
sheets.pin_desc: The 6 steps of the clinical judgment model behind every NCLEX case study: recognize cues, analyze cues, prioritize hypotheses, generate solutions, take action, evaluate outcomes. Nursing school study guide and NGN case study tips.
facts: 2. Analyze cues: what could it mean?
sheets.caption: Every NCLEX case study walks through the same 6 steps. Learn the question each step asks and you'll know what every item wants. Which step trips you up most?

sheets.title: Prioritization: Who First?
sheets.hook: Who do you see FIRST? The priority ladder
sheets.pin_title: NCLEX Prioritization Cheat Sheet: Who Do You See First?
sheets.pin_desc: NCLEX prioritization rules: airway, breathing, circulation, disability, safety. Acute over chronic, unstable over stable, actual over potential. Nursing student cheat sheet with practice questions.
sheets.caption: Stuck between two clients? Climb the ladder: airway, breathing, circulation, neuro, safety. Then the tie-breakers: acute over chronic, unstable over stable, actual over potential.

sheets.title: Delegation & Assignment
sheets.hook: What can you delegate? Remember EAT
sheets.pin_title: Nursing Delegation Made Easy: RN vs LPN vs UAP (EAT Rule)
sheets.pin_desc: NCLEX delegation rules: the RN keeps Evaluate, Assess, Teach (EAT). What LPNs and UAPs can and can't do, plus the 5 rights of delegation. Nursing school cheat sheet.
facts: + unstable clients stay with the RN
sheets.caption: Delegation in 3 letters: EAT. The RN keeps Evaluate, Assess and Teach, plus any unstable client. You can delegate tasks, never accountability.

sheets.title: Infection Prevention
sheets.hook: Contact vs droplet vs airborne in 20 seconds
sheets.pin_title: Isolation Precautions Cheat Sheet: Contact, Droplet, Airborne
sheets.pin_desc: Contact, droplet and airborne precautions for the NCLEX, plus PPE donning and doffing order. Airborne: My Chicken Hez TB (measles, chickenpox, disseminated zoster, TB). C. diff needs soap and water.
sheets.caption: Airborne precautions = "My Chicken Hez TB." N95, negative-pressure room, door closed. And for C. diff: soap and water, because alcohol rub doesn't kill spores.

sheets.title: Safety & Restraints
sheets.hook: Restraint rules the NCLEX loves
sheets.pin_title: Restraints, Fall Prevention & Fire Safety (RACE, PASS) for NCLEX
sheets.pin_desc: Nursing safety cheat sheet: restraint rules (never PRN, tie to bed frame, quick-release knot, two fingers), fall prevention, RACE and PASS fire safety, disaster triage colors and client positioning.
facts: Tie to bed frame, quick-release knot
sheets.caption: Restraints: least restrictive first, never a PRN order, tie to the bed frame (not the side rail) with a quick-release knot, and two fingers should fit under it.

sheets.title: Therapeutic Communication
sheets.hook: Never ask a client "why?" Here's why
sheets.pin_title: Therapeutic Communication NCLEX Cheat Sheet: Do's and Don'ts
sheets.pin_desc: Therapeutic vs non-therapeutic communication for the NCLEX with examples: reflecting, open-ended questions, silence, presenting reality vs false reassurance, asking why, giving advice.
sheets.caption: The best NCLEX communication answer usually names the client's feeling first. Rule out false reassurance, "why" questions and advice-giving.

sheets.title: CBC & Coagulation
sheets.hook: Heparin vs warfarin labs, finally clear
sheets.pin_title: CBC & Coag Lab Values for Nursing: Heparin aPTT vs Warfarin INR
sheets.pin_desc: Nursing lab values cheat sheet: WBC, hemoglobin, hematocrit, platelets, PT/INR and aPTT. Heparin = aPTT = protamine. Warfarin = PT/INR = vitamin K. Platelet danger zones and neutropenic precautions.
sheets.caption: "WePT": Warfarin = PT/INR, reversed with vitamin K. Heparin gets the other one: aPTT, reversed with protamine.

sheets.title: Chemistry Panel
sheets.hook: The lab values you need to know cold
sheets.pin_title: Nursing Lab Values Cheat Sheet: Chemistry Panel (Na, K, Ca, BUN)
sheets.pin_desc: Must-know chemistry lab values for nursing school and the NCLEX: sodium 135–145, potassium 3.5–5.0, calcium, magnesium, BUN, creatinine, fasting glucose 70–100, liver enzymes, troponin, BNP and HbA1c. Ranges vary by lab.
sheets.caption: Sodium 135–145. Potassium 3.5–5.0. Fasting glucose 70–100. These show up everywhere on the NCLEX. (Ranges vary slightly by lab; follow your program.)

sheets.title: Therapeutic Drug Levels
sheets.hook: Narrow window drugs: easy to overdose
sheets.pin_title: Therapeutic Drug Levels for Nursing: Digoxin, Lithium, Phenytoin
sheets.pin_desc: Therapeutic drug level ranges and toxicity signs for nursing: digoxin 0.5–2.0, lithium 0.6–1.2, phenytoin 10–20, vancomycin trough, gentamicin peak and trough. Common teaching ranges.
facts: Low K⁺ raises digoxin toxicity risk
sheets.caption: Digoxin, lithium, phenytoin: tiny gap between helpful and toxic. Digoxin toxicity = nausea, yellow-green halos, bradycardia. Low potassium makes it worse.

sheets.title: ABG Interpretation
sheets.hook: ABGs in 3 steps (ROME)
sheets.pin_title: How to Interpret ABGs in 3 Steps: ROME Method for Nursing
sheets.pin_desc: Easy ABG interpretation for nursing students: normal values (pH 7.35–7.45, PaCO2 35–45, HCO3 22–26), the ROME mnemonic, compensation and 4 practice ABGs with answers.
sheets.caption: ABGs in 3 steps: look at the pH, find the value that matches, check for compensation. ROME does the rest: Respiratory Opposite, Metabolic Equal.

sheets.title: Potassium & Sodium
sheets.hook: Potassium = the heart. Sodium = the brain.
sheets.pin_title: Hypokalemia vs Hyperkalemia & Sodium Imbalances: Nursing Cheat Sheet
sheets.pin_desc: Potassium and sodium imbalances for the NCLEX: hypokalemia flat T waves and U waves, hyperkalemia peaked T waves, never IV push potassium, SIADH hyponatremia, diabetes insipidus hypernatremia.
facts: Low K⁺: flat T, U wave
High K⁺: tall peaked T, wide QRS
Never give IV potassium by push
sheets.caption: Low potassium = low and slow: weak muscles, flat T waves, U waves. High potassium = tall peaked T waves. And IV potassium is NEVER given by IV push.

sheets.title: Calcium, Magnesium & Phosphorus
sheets.hook: Stones, bones, groans: high calcium
sheets.pin_title: Calcium & Magnesium Imbalances: Chvostek, Trousseau, Mag Toxicity
sheets.pin_desc: Hypocalcemia (Chvostek and Trousseau signs, after thyroidectomy), hypercalcemia (stones, bones, groans), hypomagnesemia and hypermagnesemia with calcium gluconate as the antidote. Nursing cheat sheet.
sheets.caption: Post-thyroidectomy client with tingling lips? Think low calcium. Chvostek (tap the cheek) and Trousseau (BP cuff) are your signs.

sheets.title: IV Fluids & Fluid Balance
sheets.hook: Isotonic vs hypotonic vs hypertonic
sheets.pin_title: IV Fluids Cheat Sheet: Isotonic, Hypotonic, Hypertonic for Nursing
sheets.pin_desc: IV fluid types for nursing school: 0.9% NS, lactated Ringer's, D5W, 0.45% NaCl, 3% saline. Fluid volume deficit vs excess, IV complications and blood transfusion essentials.
facts: Hypertonic: pulls water OUT of cells
sheets.caption: Hypo = cells swell. Hyper = cells shrink. And normal saline is the only fluid that goes with blood products.

sheets.title: Drug Suffix Decoder
sheets.hook: Don't know the drug? Read the ending.
sheets.pin_title: Pharmacology Drug Suffixes Cheat Sheet: -olol, -pril, -sartan & More
sheets.pin_desc: Drug suffix decoder for nursing pharmacology: -olol beta blockers, -pril ACE inhibitors, -sartan ARBs, -statin, -prazole, -parin and more, with the key nursing check for each class.
sheets.caption: Never seen the drug before? Read the ending. -olol = beta blocker, -pril = ACE inhibitor, -sartan = ARB, -statin = cholesterol. Save this for pharm.

sheets.title: Cardiac Medications
sheets.hook: Check this before EVERY cardiac med
sheets.pin_title: Cardiac Meds for Nursing: Digoxin, Beta Blockers, ACE, Nitro
sheets.pin_desc: Cardiac medications nursing cheat sheet: digoxin apical pulse for 1 full minute, beta blockers mask hypoglycemia, ACE inhibitor cough and angioedema, nitroglycerin rules, loop vs thiazide vs potassium-sparing diuretics.
sheets.caption: Before digoxin: apical pulse for a full minute, hold if under 60. Toxicity looks like nausea, vomiting and yellow-green halos.

sheets.title: Anticoagulants & Antidotes
sheets.hook: The antidote list you need to memorize
sheets.pin_title: Antidotes Cheat Sheet for Nursing: Naloxone, Protamine, Vitamin K
sheets.pin_desc: Nursing antidote list: opioids–naloxone, benzodiazepines–flumazenil, acetaminophen–acetylcysteine, heparin–protamine, warfarin–vitamin K, magnesium–calcium gluconate, digoxin–digoxin immune fab.
sheets.caption: The antidote list: opioids → naloxone, benzos → flumazenil, acetaminophen → acetylcysteine, heparin → protamine, warfarin → vitamin K. Naloxone can wear off before the opioid does, so keep watching breathing.

sheets.title: Insulin & Diabetes Meds
sheets.hook: Peak time = highest hypo risk
sheets.pin_title: Insulin Chart for Nursing: Onset, Peak, Duration + Clear Before Cloudy
sheets.pin_desc: Insulin types for nursing school: rapid, short (regular), intermediate (NPH), long-acting. Onset, peak and duration, mixing clear before cloudy, the rule of 15 for hypoglycemia, and non-insulin diabetes meds.
facts: Regular is the insulin given IV
Hypo rule of 15: 15 g, recheck in 15
sheets.caption: Mixing insulin? Clear before cloudy: draw up regular, then NPH. And hypoglycemia is "cold and clammy, need some candy."

sheets.title: High-Alert, Psych & Anti-Infective Meds
sheets.hook: Small mistakes, big harm: high-alert meds
sheets.pin_title: High-Alert & Psych Meds for Nursing: Opioids, Lithium, SSRIs, MAOIs
sheets.pin_desc: Nursing pharmacology cheat sheet: opioid respiratory depression, antipsychotic EPS and NMS, SSRI and serotonin syndrome, MAOI tyramine foods, lithium toxicity, vancomycin and TB drugs.
sheets.caption: MAOIs + aged cheese = hypertensive crisis. Antipsychotic + high fever and rigidity = neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Save these psych pharm red flags.

sheets.title: Cardiac
sheets.hook: Left = Lungs. Right = the Rest.
sheets.pin_title: Left vs Right Heart Failure + Heart Rhythms for Nursing
sheets.pin_desc: Left vs right sided heart failure made simple, MI signs (atypical in women), and must-know rhythms: atrial fibrillation, SVT, VT, VF and asystole with the priority action for each.
facts: Left → Lungs: crackles, pink frothy sputum
Right → Rest of body: JVD, edema
Asystole: CPR + epi. Do not shock.
sheets.caption: Left-sided heart failure backs up into the Lungs. Right-sided backs up into the Rest of the body. That's it. That's the trick.

sheets.title: Respiratory
sheets.hook: Restlessness = early sign of hypoxia
sheets.pin_title: Respiratory Nursing Cheat Sheet: COPD, Asthma, Chest Tubes
sheets.pin_desc: Respiratory nursing review: asthma vs COPD, COPD SpO2 target 88–92%, early vs late hypoxia signs, chest tube care and troubleshooting, ventilator alarms and suctioning rules.
sheets.caption: Restlessness and anxiety are EARLY signs of hypoxia. Cyanosis is late. Don't wait for blue.

sheets.title: Endocrine
sheets.hook: DKA vs HHS: the difference
sheets.pin_title: DKA vs HHS, Thyroid, Addison's vs Cushing's: Endocrine Cheat Sheet
sheets.pin_desc: Endocrine nursing cheat sheet: DKA vs HHS comparison, DKA treatment order (fluids, check potassium, insulin), hypo vs hyperthyroid, Addison's vs Cushing's, SIADH vs diabetes insipidus.
sheets.caption: SIADH = Soaked Inside: retains water, low sodium. DI = Dry Inside: pees it all out, high sodium.

sheets.title: Neuro
sheets.hook: The earliest sign of increased ICP
sheets.pin_title: Neuro Nursing Cheat Sheet: ICP, GCS, Stroke BE FAST, Seizures
sheets.pin_desc: Neuro nursing review for the NCLEX: early vs late signs of increased ICP (Cushing's triad), Glasgow Coma Scale (8 = intubate), stroke BE FAST, seizure care and autonomic dysreflexia.
sheets.caption: The earliest sign of increased intracranial pressure is a change in level of consciousness. Cushing's triad is LATE. And GCS 8 or less: intubate.

sheets.title: Renal & GI
sheets.hook: Feel the thrill, hear the bruit
sheets.pin_title: Renal & GI Nursing Cheat Sheet: Dialysis, AV Fistula, GI Bleed
sheets.pin_desc: Renal and GI nursing review: AV fistula care (thrill and bruit, no BP in that arm), peritoneal dialysis cloudy effluent, CKD diet, appendicitis, pancreatitis, cirrhosis and GI bleeding.
facts: No BP, IVs or draws in that arm
sheets.caption: Dialysis fistula: feel the thrill, hear the bruit, and never take a BP in that arm.

sheets.title: Shock, Burns & Emergencies
sheets.hook: Parkland formula in one example
sheets.pin_title: Shock Types, Sepsis & Burns (Rule of Nines, Parkland) for Nursing
sheets.pin_desc: Shock types comparison, sepsis bundle basics, rule of nines and the Parkland formula with a worked example, compartment syndrome and fat embolism. Emergency nursing cheat sheet.
facts: Half in first 8 hr from the burn
sheets.caption: Parkland: 4 mL × kg × %TBSA of LR over 24 hours. Half in the first 8 hours from the time of the burn, not from arrival.

sheets.title: Pregnancy & Labor
sheets.hook: VEAL CHOP, the only fetal monitoring trick
sheets.pin_title: VEAL CHOP Fetal Heart Rate Decelerations + Stages of Labor
sheets.pin_desc: Maternity nursing cheat sheet: VEAL CHOP for fetal heart rate patterns, interventions for late decelerations, Naegele's rule, GTPAL, stages of labor and normal FHR 110–160.
sheets.caption: VEAL CHOP: Variable = Cord, Early = Head, Accels = OK, Late = Placenta. Late decels? Stop oxytocin, left side, IV bolus, O₂ per protocol, notify.

sheets.title: Complications, Postpartum & Newborn
sheets.hook: Boggy fundus? Do THIS first
sheets.pin_title: Postpartum Nursing Cheat Sheet: Hemorrhage, Mag Toxicity, Apgar
sheets.pin_desc: Postpartum and OB complications: preeclampsia severe features, magnesium sulfate toxicity and antidote, previa vs abruption, postpartum hemorrhage (fundal massage first), lochia stages and Apgar scoring.
sheets.caption: Boggy uterus after birth? Fundal massage first. On magnesium sulfate: check reflexes, respirations and urine output every time.

sheets.title: Pediatrics
sheets.hook: Kids compensate, then crash fast
sheets.pin_title: Pediatric Nursing Cheat Sheet: Vital Signs, Milestones, Erikson
sheets.pin_desc: Pediatric nursing review: vital signs by age, growth and motor milestones, Erikson stages and types of play, epiglottitis, croup, cystic fibrosis and Kawasaki disease.
facts: Hypotension is a LATE sign in kids
sheets.caption: Birth weight doubles by about 5–6 months and triples by 12. And in kids, low blood pressure is a late sign of shock: tachycardia comes first.

sheets.title: Mental Health Essentials
sheets.hook: Alcohol withdrawal timeline
sheets.pin_title: Mental Health Nursing Cheat Sheet: Withdrawal, Suicide Risk, Defenses
sheets.pin_desc: Psych nursing review: suicide risk assessment, alcohol withdrawal timeline (seizures 12–48 hr, DTs 48–72 hr), thiamine before glucose, defense mechanisms, anxiety levels and de-escalation.
sheets.caption: Alcohol withdrawal: tremors at 6–24 hours, seizures at 12–48, delirium tremens at 48–72+. And give thiamine before glucose.

sheets.title: Dosage Calculations
sheets.hook: Dosage calc: one formula does most of it
sheets.pin_title: Nursing Dosage Calculations Cheat Sheet: Formulas + Worked Examples
sheets.pin_desc: Dosage calculation formulas for nursing school: desired over have times volume, IV rate mL/hr, drip rate gtt/min, weight-based dosing and conversions, with 6 worked examples.
sheets.caption: Most dosage calc questions are just Desired ÷ Have × Volume. Label your units and round only the final answer.

quizzes.question: Which client does the nurse see first?
options: A. Post-op, pain 6/10, asking for meds
C. 2 days post-thyroidectomy, tingling around the mouth
quizzes.why: Perioral tingling after thyroidectomy suggests low calcium, which can progress to tetany, laryngospasm and seizures. The others are expected or stable.
quizzes.caption: Who do you see first? Comment your answer before the reveal. Prioritization is the biggest slice of the NCLEX.

quizzes.question: Which client does the nurse see first?
options: A. New cast, toes numb and pale
C. Post-op day 1, no BM in 3 days
quizzes.why: Numbness and pallor below a cast suggest impaired circulation or compartment syndrome: limb-threatening. The rest can wait.
quizzes.caption: Numb, pale toes under a new cast. Would you have picked it? Drop your answer below.

quizzes.question: Before a mastectomy, a client says: "I don't know how my husband will look at me after this." Best response?
options: A. "Your husband loves you. He won't care."
B. "Why do you think he'll feel differently?"
C. "You're worried about how this will affect your relationship."
quizzes.why: Reflecting names her feeling and keeps her talking. A is false reassurance, B asks "why," D jumps to a solution she didn't ask for.
quizzes.caption: Therapeutic communication check. Which one did you pick?

quizzes.question: pH 7.30 · PaCO₂ 58 · HCO₃⁻ 25. What is it?
quizzes.why: pH low and CO₂ high move in opposite directions: respiratory (ROME). HCO₃⁻ is still normal, so it's uncompensated. Think opioid overdose or COPD exacerbation.
quizzes.caption: ABG in 10 seconds with ROME. Comment your answer, then watch the reveal.
